codes.meaning: Restricted airflow — the lint screen or vent is clogged, or the vent is crushed, kinked, or has too many turns.

AF.why_it_happens: A clogged lint screen or vent, or a duct that is crushed, kinked or has too many turns.
AF.what_to_try: Clean the lint screen, clear the duct run to the outside wall, and check the vent flap opens when the dryer runs.
AF.when_to_call: If the run is genuinely clear and it returns, the airflow sensor needs checking.

codes.meaning: Low or no line voltage; there may be a problem with the home's power supply keeping the heater from turning on.
The drying cycle was interrupted by a power failure.

PF.what_it_means: Not a fault. The drying cycle was interrupted by a power failure.
PF.why_it_happens: An outage, a tripped breaker, or the plug pulled mid-cycle.
PF.what_to_try: Restart the cycle. If it recurs with no outage you can account for, check the breaker and whether the dryer shares a loaded circuit.
PF.when_to_call: If PF keeps appearing on a stable supply, the power board is worth checking.

codes.meaning: Primary control board failure.

F01.what_it_means: The primary control board has failed.
F01.why_it_happens: An electronic failure rather than anything to do with how the dryer is used.
F01.what_to_try: A power-cycle at the breaker clears a one-off glitch; a code that returns is naming a real board fault.
F01.when_to_call: If it comes back after a power cycle, the board needs replacing.

codes.meaning: Exhaust thermistor fault.
Drive motor fault.

range.note: Maytag documents wall ovens and ranges under one combined support page; oven and range share this source.

codes.meaning: The range's control board has detected a wiring or power-supply problem at the outlet, or picked up electrical noise during a brief outage.
The control panel has been deliberately locked, so the keypad won't respond until it's unlocked.
The range is reporting that it lost electrical power at some point and needs the clock/settings reset.
Sabbath Mode has been turned on, suppressing normal tones, lights, and some display behavior for religious observance.
The range has entered its built-in calibration routine for adjusting oven temperature accuracy.
Not a fault — the display is set to show temperature in Celsius rather than Fahrenheit.
The fridge detected a power interruption severe enough that the freezer warmed to 18°F or higher.
The control board has hit an internal fault condition; Maytag's own fix is a full power-cycle before considering it a service issue.
The unit sensed the fresh-food section above roughly 48°F or the freezer above roughly 15°F for more than 90 minutes.
A door or drawer was left open past a model-specific threshold while cooling was active.
The unit's cooling function has been manually switched off.
The water filter has reached or is nearing its recommended service life.
The control panel has been locked on purpose, so buttons won't respond until it's unlocked.
The washer can't detect that a detergent cartridge is loaded in the dispenser.
The machine has sensed an excessive amount of suds and is pausing or adjusting the cycle to clear them.
The door/lid isn't latching securely, so the control won't proceed with the cycle.

F5 E2.what_it_means: The door or lid is not latching securely, so the control will not start the cycle.
F5 E2.why_it_happens: Laundry caught in the opening, or a strike and latch that are no longer meeting properly.
F5 E2.what_to_try: Clear anything caught around the seal and close firmly. Check the strike the latch engages for damage.
F5 E2.when_to_call: If a clear doorway still will not lock, the lid lock assembly is the usual cause.

codes.meaning: The washer isn't seeing enough incoming water flow to fill or run the selected cycle normally.
The tub is taking unusually long to drain — roughly eight minutes or more triggers it.

F9 E1.what_it_means: The tub is taking unusually long to drain -- roughly eight minutes or more triggers the code.
F9 E1.why_it_happens: Normally a restriction in the drain path rather than a failed part: a kinked hose, a standpipe that cannot take the flow, or debris in the pump.
F9 E1.what_to_try: Straighten the drain hose, check it is not inserted too far into the standpipe, and clear the pump filter if your model has one you can reach.
F9 E1.when_to_call: If the drain path is clear and it still times out, the pump needs testing.

codes.meaning: Water has been detected pooling in the drip tray beneath the dishwasher.

F8E4.what_it_means: Water has been detected pooling in the drip tray beneath the dishwasher.
F8E4.why_it_happens: Something above the tray is leaking — a seal, a hose connection or the tub itself.
F8E4.what_to_try: Turn the water supply off at the valve and stop using the machine.
F8E4.when_to_call: This needs a technician — the code reports water where it should not be, not its source.

codes.meaning: The wash motor is reporting a malfunction.
The dishwasher is taking far longer than normal to drain, or isn't draining at all.

F9E1.what_it_means: The dishwasher is taking far longer than normal to drain, or is not draining at all.
F9E1.why_it_happens: Usually a clogged tub filter, a kinked drain hose, or an air gap that has silted up.
F9E1.what_to_try: Clear the tub filter, check the air gap, then the drain hose for kinks.
F9E1.when_to_call: If the filter and hose are clear and it still will not drain, the drain pump needs testing.

codes.meaning: There's a communication or logic fault between the user interface and the main control board.
The dishwasher isn't sensing that water has entered the tub.

oven.note: Maytag documents wall ovens and ranges under one combined support page; oven and range share this source.

codes.meaning: The oven's control board has detected a wiring or power-supply problem at the outlet, or electrical noise during a brief outage.
The control panel has been deliberately locked and won't respond to the keypad until unlocked.
The oven has entered its built-in calibration routine for fine-tuning temperature accuracy.
Sabbath Mode is active, suppressing normal tones, lights, and certain display behavior.
The oven is reporting it lost electrical power and needs its clock/settings re-entered.
The oven's way of showing the clock needs to be reset after a power interruption, not a hardware fault.
